packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET-12 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
this text. One thing the images themselves show: a modern pencil note on the
upper margin of face 1, something like "Fr(?) Nr(?). 6 (3890)" or "F14 N.6
(3896)" - evidently a modern shelf/inventory note; I record it as visible and
infer nothing from it. I opened only PROMPT.md and the six image files of this
packet (file names came from one directory listing of the packet directories;
packet.json was not opened).

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Images
  Face 1: image-001 (overview with ruler), image-002 (left tile), image-003
          (right tile).
  Face 2: image-004 (overview with ruler), image-005 (left tile), image-006
          (right tile).
The tiles are small (under 1000 px wide for c. 7 cm of leaf), so the script is
only a few pixels high; this, not the leaf, is the main limit on the reading.

Observations
- One horizontal parchment strip, c. 14 cm wide and c. 3 cm high by the ruler,
  cut from the TOP of a leaf: a blank upper margin of c. 1 cm is preserved
  above the first line on both faces, and the lower edge is a ragged cut
  through the 6th line.
- Two columns on each face, c. 5.5-6 cm wide each, with a narrow
  intercolumnar space. 5 full lines + the tops of a 6th survive in each
  column. Outer margin blank (face 1 right, face 2 left).
- Script: a very small, compressed, heavily abbreviated gothic bookhand in
  dark ink, with frequent suspension strokes, 2-shaped r, tironian et, and
  many points between short clauses.
- Red: small red paragraph marks / red-touched letters inside the lines
  (face 1 col. a L1, L2, L4, L5; col. b L1, L2, L4, L5). Face 2 col. a opens
  with a red initial two lines high at the top left (I read it as P or O;
  see below) with a red vertical line or flourish running down the margin
  beside it. Face 2 col. b line 5 has a short word in red (rubric) after the
  end of a sentence, and red marks at the line below.
- Face 1 col. b has a short group ("ml'"/"ns'" or similar) written above the
  first line at its left end: either an interlinear correction or the tail of
  a run-over; no other gloss, no running title, no underlining visible.
- Face 2 is browner and more stained than face 1.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- The paragraph marks followed by formulae that look like "Ad ... q(uae)rit(ur)"
  / "Item" / "S(ed)" suggest scholastic prose arranged as short questions and
  replies or as a chain of notes on successive points. The red initial at the
  top of face 2 col. a and the red word in face 2 col. b suggest section
  openings. Which face is recto is not determinable from the strip (the outer
  margin positions suggest face 1 = one side with outer margin at right, face
  2 = the other side, as expected, but not recto/verso).

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: all five full lines of each of the four columns, since so little
survives. The cut 6th line of each column is not read. Where the tile
resolution does not let me separate minims I say so.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers count the written lines from the top of the named tile; in every
tile L1 is the first line of the column (top of the leaf).

--- FACE 1, column a (image-002) ---
image-002 L1: Qꝛ(?) octo(?) dicunt(ur)(?) ſ(?). [red mark] ext(re)ma(?) ſpei ſc̄(?) p̄ſumpc̄o(?) ⁊ deſp(er)ac̄o(?) · timoris(?)
image-002 L2: ⁊(?) temeritas(?) ⁊ timiditas(?). ¶(red) o(mn)ia(?) p(e)cc(at)a(?) fug(?). illa ult(im)a(?). timoꝛ
image-002 L3: a(?)̄ tenet mediū(?). [.] qꝛ(?) ſpes ē(?) de b̄titudi(n)e(?) q̄(?) n̄ ſ[..]t(?). timoꝛ ⁊ ſpe(?)
image-002 L4: n̄ ſ̄t(?) ꝯ̄rioꝝ(?). ſic ſ(?)[..]lac̄o(?) ī p̄ma(?). ¶(red) Ad(?) q̄rit(ur)(?) q̄ fuīt(?) mater-(?)
image-002 L5: [..]i cād(?) ē(?) ill(us)(?) cognoſcens(?). ¶(red) ſꝫ n̄ iqūt(?) ſc̄(?) hūꝫ(?) uſum(?) tene(re)(?)
image-002 L6: [upper halves only; "...bon(?)... malu(?)..." possible]
Confidence notes, col. a: "ſpei", "p̄ſump-", "⁊ deſp-", "timiditas", "tenet
mediū", "timoꝛ" (twice), "cognoſcen-" are the firmest shapes. "octo",
"ext(re)ma", "temeritas", "o(mn)ia p(e)cc(at)a", "b̄titudine", "mater-" are
plausible letter-counts but not secure at this resolution.

--- FACE 1, column b (image-003; its left edge overlaps the right edge of
image-002, where the first 2-4 letters of each col. b line also appear - same
text, not additional) ---
image-003 (above L1, at left): ml'(?) / nſ'(?)   [small group above the line]
image-003 L1: ca(?). d(icitu)r(?) [red touch] fruis(?). n̄ q̄ſtip(?)[..]ns(?). ſꝫ q̄ſi(?) ꝑuoīs(?). qꝛ ꝑ pl'eto(?) ſūt(?) man-
image-003 L2: data(?) ⁊(red?) ꝯſilia(?). q̄ ad ip̄am(?) tendūt(?) o(mn)ia cet(er)a(?) q̄ ſc̄(?) ī p̄cepto(?) vir(?)-
image-003 L3: pag̃s(?) ītas(?) et ad nexo(?). n̄(red?) ut heāt(?). ſꝫ ut mag̃(?) heāt(?) vn(?)
image-003 L4: cōe(?). ꝗꝛ(?) eōe(?) mō(?) adhuc h̄uēnt(?). ¶(red) Itē(?) p̄(?) diſtīctōs(?) o(mn)i(?)l(?)
image-003 L5: a b̄ c̄(?) d̄(?). ſꝫ q̄ ueni(?)ē(?) fidei ⁊ ſpei. ſꝫ mag̃(?) ꝓ(?). X̄(?). coꝛde(?) tū(?)
image-003 L6: [upper halves only]
Confidence notes, col. b: "man|data ⁊ ꝯſilia" (across L1-L2), "tendūt",
"ī p̄cepto", "adhuc", "fidei ⁊ ſpei", "ſꝫ ut mag̃" are the firmest. L3 opening
and L1 "fruis ... q̄ſtip..ns ... ꝑuoīs" are letter-shapes I could not resolve
into words.
Upper margin above col. b: modern pencil note (see exposure statement).

--- FACE 2, column a (image-005) ---
image-005 L1: [red initial, 2 lines high: P(?)/O(?)]oſt(?) h(?)[.] vidēꝫ(?) de cogni(ti)o(n)e(?) d(e)i(?) q̄ hab(?)u(?)[..]t(?) [..]giniciles(?)
image-005 L2: [indented beside the initial] h̄eant(?) fidē(?). ⁊ diſcip(u)li(?) adhuc īſtruūt(ur)(?). dic(it)(?) ap(osto)l(u)s(?) q(?)
image-005 L3: ph(ilosoph)i(?) loſop(?)[..] d(omi)n(u)m(?) et cogno(?)[..]t(?). ſꝫ n̄ ſic(ut)(?) d(eu)m(?) gl(or)ificauer(un)t(?)
image-005 L4: ⁊(?) ang(?)[..] [..] q̄ magi(?) [..]ōs(?) defec(er)ūt(?) ī tc̄o(?) ſigno. qꝛ(?)
image-005 L5: [.]h(?)i[.]lſop(?)hi(?) de p̄re(?) ⁊ filio cognouer(un)t(?). ſꝫ de ſp̄u(?) ſc̄o(?)
image-005 L6: [upper halves only]
A red vertical stroke runs down the left margin beside L1-L5.
Confidence notes: "de cogni..e", "adhuc", "gl..ificauer..", "defec.. ī tc̄o
ſigno", "⁊ filio cognouer..", "ſꝫ de ſ.. ſ.." are the firmest shapes. The
opening word after the initial, and L4's first half, are not secure.

--- FACE 2, column b (image-006; its left edge overlaps the right edge of
image-005 - same text) ---
image-006 L1: Ad(?) q̄(?) [red touch] thomas(?) uidit(?). R(?)eſc̄ons(?) q̄(?) uidiſ(ti)(?) ⁊ c̄(?). ſꝫ p̄ſum(?)ent(?)[..]
image-006 L2: ſem(?)[..] [red touch] thomas(?) n̄ uidebat actu de(?)[.] ſine ue(?) lateret(?)
image-006 L3: ⁊ ḡ(?) [.]ocū(?) ibat(?) cū pat(re)(?) [red touch] ut(?) cognoſcebat ⁊ vuln̄a(?) ⁊ fixur(?)[.]s(?).
image-006 L4: [..]credebat(?) [..] ſic intellig̃dū(?) ſic p̄t(?) ee(?) ḡ(?) ſine gl̄o(?). iſte(?)
image-006 L5: [..] hoc credid(?)[..] ⁊ fid(?)[.]. [word in RED, c. 6-7 letters, "In[..]ipit(?)"/illegible]
image-006 L6: [upper halves only, with red marks at the left]
Confidence notes: "n̄ uidebat actu", "cognoſcebat", "intellig̃dū", "hoc cred-"
are the firmest. The name-like word read "thomas(?)" in L1 and L2 is the same
shape twice (t/c + h + 4-5 letters ending in s); I give it as a shape reading
only and have NOT used it to infer anything about the text.

4. LIMITATIONS
- Image resolution: the native tiles give only about 6-8 pixels of x-height.
  Abbreviation strokes are visible as strokes but often not attributable to a
  particular letter; minim counts are approximate. Nearly every expansion
  above is therefore tentative, and I have marked the few firmer ones.
- The strip preserves only the top 5 lines of each column; text does not run
  on between the bottom of one column and the top of the next (c. the whole
  column height is lost between them), so the four spans are disconnected.
- Recto/verso order of the two faces is not established.
- Higher-resolution tiles of each column (at least 3-4x the present scale)
  would allow a much firmer reading; the script itself looks well preserved
  on face 1 and moderately stained on face 2.
- This is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the stated rules
  other than the directory listing noted above.
